Good morning. The most interesting thread today is selective, activation-level defenses beating blunt filters for prompt injection and jailbreaks, with a second arc around trajectory-aware evaluation/guarding for long-horizon agents, and a side channel on adapter- and skill-supply-chain risk.

BASIS lands the headline for LLM security: instead of treating every whiff of injection as grounds to refuse, it reads the prefill attention and uses two tiny linear probes to decide (a) is there an injection attempt and (b) will it actually breach this instruction template. The Attention Competition Ratio signals are cheap, model-side, and plug into a cascaded gate—no extra LLM calls. On six open models and mixed tasks they get near-perfect detection while sharply cutting over-refusal on “safe attack” samples, especially under robust instruction templates. If you’re tuning agents with strict-but-costly refuse policies, this looks like an immediate way to buy back utility without opening the floodgates. It also pairs naturally with trajectory-level UQ for deciding when to spend a guarded call vs. proceed.

Two red-teamers push in opposite directions and bracket what “realistic” attackers can do. PIMiner learns a portable strategy library across datasets and target models, then transfers it with ~10 queries per case, posting high ASR on IPIArena and AgentDojo and beating RL-based approaches that don’t generalize. SAVOR goes more austere: one-shot indirect prompt injection via outcome-conditioned reflection over offline trajectories, then emits a single payload on an unseen target, outperforming prior attacks by 2.5–11.8 points and transferring across defenses. Together they stress-test both your budgeted online defenses and your single-interaction harness hardening.

If you worry your detection signals are measuring the wrong thing, “Measuring the Wrong Thing” is a sobering replication: pre-generation harmful-intent scores can anti-rank actual jailbreak success once wrappers are introduced; outcome AUROC even flips sign for wrapped harmful prompts. They propose a content-independent coordinate via Active Attention Probing and show calibration crumbles under distribution shift before ranking does. This dovetails neatly with BASIS: model-internal, location-aware probes and per-sample breach prediction are the way out of proxy traps.

On the feature-interpretability flank, Feature Nonlocality gives a label-free measure—entropy of per-position influence—for how “abstract” an SAE feature is. High-FNL features align with contextual reasoning, and steering them bumps MATH-500 on DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B by 4.6 points over low-FNL steering. More importantly for security, auditing jailbreak-mitigation features shows many are low-FNL and positional—i.e., brittle triggers rather than robust abstractions. If you’re investing in steering as a defense or capability edit, this is a crisp triage tool for what to steer.

Persistent Semantic Entities formalizes what many of us have anecdotally seen in tool-augmented pipelines: name binding is the necessary and dominant lever for long-lived contamination that jumps components and sessions. Preference and instruction contamination persist almost undiminished; persona decays; factual injection is model-dependent. A context-isolated self-verifier reduces contamination far more reliably than keyword detectors, and contamination compounds through multi-stage pipelines (roughly doubling across four stages). This is a concrete argument for name-binding audits, identity rotation, and isolation gates between tools/memory layers—plus a better baseline than regexes.

Supply-chain risk shows up twice. ElasticBack plants a weight-free, conditional backdoor in a single agent skill by coupling a benign-looking trigger in user queries with a malicious rule in the skill doc; it achieves high ASR with near-zero FPR, preserves clean accuracy, and evades deployment defenses while transferring across models. LoRAScan, in turn, offers a practical adapter-side defense: monitor a small subset of LoRA insertion sites whose down-projection activations are stable on clean inputs but spike under triggers. Pre-identify them offline, then reject at runtime; they report ~98% malicious-input rejection with low benign error across benchmarks. Taken together: skills and adapters are the soft underbelly—instrument both.

For long-horizon agents, the Horizon Gap survey is the best single map I’ve seen recently. It cleanly separates long-horizon vs. long-context vs. long-term memory, and makes a hard claim you’ll recognize: as horizons stretch, outcome-only signals go information-poor, so you must manufacture dense process-level signals and credit assignment. They catalog where measurement is failing—especially decomposing model vs. harness capability and bias in process-level judges—and tee up an agenda for denser diagnostics. This frames why trajectory-aware defenses like DreamGuard matter: its risk-aware world model forecasts near-future latent risk and intervenes pre-tool with 25 ms overhead, beating reactive/proactive baselines on safety–utility trade-offs. If you’re wiring guardrails into multi-hour jobs, combine Horizon Gap’s measurement cautions with DreamGuard-like low-latency forecasters and BASIS-style prefill gates.

Outside your usual lane, but worth a look for time-series foundations and cost/security trade-offs: Matryoshka Language Model Suites train nested sub-models end-to-end, enabling step-wise distillation and cleaner speculative decoding because the draft lives inside the verifier. They match baseline quality with 36% less training compute and deliver 14–26% higher speculative throughput. If you’re maintaining both LLM and TSFM stacks, the “suite-as-one-checkpoint” idea plus matryoshka-style elasticity can simplify governance, telemetry, and on-device/private deployments where you want predictable behavior across sizes.

If you have room for one more adjacent signal: Personalized Federated Sparse Adaptation for TSFMs shows a practical recipe—heterogeneous temporal MoE adapters with client-aware routing—that consistently beats global FL and local-only training on non-IID energy data. The finding that best sparse strategies are backbone- and metric-dependent mirrors the “don’t overgeneralize recipes” lesson from LLM harnesses, and it’s relevant if you’re contemplating privacy-preserving TSFM adaptation alongside secure LLM agents at the edge.

Net: favor internal, location-stable signals over intent proxies (BASIS, AAP), treat one-shot and low-budget IPI as first-class attacker models (SAVOR, PIMiner), harden the supply chain at the adapter/skill boundary (LoRAScan, ElasticBack), and move safety to the trajectory level for long horizons (Horizon Gap, DreamGuard). Matryoshka suites and federated sparse adapters round out an efficiency/governance play that pays off in both your LLM and TSFM lines.

stories.title: BASIS: Breach-Aware Selective Prompt Injection Shielding with Prefill Attention Probes
stories.summary: The paper addresses over-refusal in prompt-injection defenses by noting that aligned models with robust instructions can withstand many injections, so blanket detection-and-refuse strategies are suboptimal. It proposes BASIS, which uses Attention Competition Ratio features to train two sparse linear probes—an existence probe and a breach probe—that operate in a cascaded, no-extra-inference gating pipeline to detect injections, predict per-sample breaches, and assess instruction robustness. Experiments on four tasks and six open-source LLMs report near-perfect injection detection with substantially reduced over-refusal on safe attack samples, particularly when using robust instruction templates.
stories.why_it_matters: It introduces a lightweight, prefill-attention–based, per-sample breach predictor that can cut false refusals without extra LLM calls, complementing existing prompt-injection defenses and aligning with selective prediction ideas familiar from LLM safety and reliability.
stories.reason: Persistent semantic entities expose long-lived, cross-boundary contamination in tool-augmented agents — directly relevant to agentic attack surfaces, memory poisoning, and debugging for security.

stories.title: Measuring Semantic Abstractness of SAE Features via Nonlocality
stories.summary: The paper introduces Feature Nonlocality (FNL), defined as the entropy of the normalized per-position influence on an SAE feature’s activation, as a metric for semantic abstractness. FNL correlates with LLM-based proxy metrics and distinguishes contextual reasoning features from token-driven ones, assigning higher FNL to the contextual feature in 73–84% of mixed pairs. Applications include auditing jailbreak-mitigation features (finding many are low-FNL positional features) and showing that steering high-FNL features can boost MATH-500 accuracy by 4.6 points in DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B, outperforming low-FNL steering though gains are model-specific.
stories.why_it_matters: Offers an LLM-independent, label-free criterion to identify genuinely abstract SAE features, informing safer jailbreak defenses and more effective feature steering for reasoning tasks.
stories.reason: Systematic review of vulnerabilities in agentic LLMs directly maps to the reader's primary interest in agent attack surfaces, tool/memory manipulation, and the state of red-teaming and mitigation research.

stories.title: From Runnable to Verifiable: An Independent Reproducibility Study of LLM/Agent-Driven Vulnerability Validation Artifacts
stories.summary: This pre-registered reproducibility audit examines LLM/agent-driven vulnerability validation artifacts across 104 papers (2023–2026), finding only 59 with publicly reachable artifacts and executing 18 paper-level workflows and 102 anchor benchmark cases. It reports high mismatch and fragility: 58/102 anchor cases have internal CVE IDs diverging from directory labels; only 10/18 artifacts run end-to-end at R0 (11/18 after R1 env-only fixes); and embedded oracles are unreliable, with 20/30 patched-counterfactuals still signaling and 7/19 negative controls triggering, yielding oracle sensitivity 60% and specificity 45%. The study argues that vulnerable-build triggers are not CVE-specific evidence without a clean patched counterfactual and offers a reusable, pre-registered protocol (post-conditions, R0/R1 repair ladder, G1–G3 evidence levels, patched-counterfactual oracles) for the community.
stories.why_it_matters: It surfaces concrete failure modes and a reusable protocol for verifying LLM/agent security claims—directly informing eval design, oracle construction, and counterfactual controls for both LLM security and time-series-style benchmark reproducibility.
stories.reason: ActBench proposes an execution-trajectory-based behavioral safety benchmark for cowork agents, directly applicable to evaluating agent risks like data leakage and unauthorized actions—highly relevant for tooling and red-teaming.

stories.title: Agent Against Agent: An Agentic System for Automatic Prompt Injection Red Teaming
stories.summary: The paper proposes PIMiner, an agentic red-teaming system for prompt injection that trains over sequences of (dataset, target model) pairs to build a strategy library from scratch. At test time, it transfers this library to unseen target LLMs without additional training and uses only a small number of target-agent queries per sample (e.g., 10). Experiments show strong ASR on IPIArena (76.2% Gemini-2.5-Pro, 61.9% GPT-5.1, 42.9% Claude-Sonnet-4.5) and AgentDojo (86.7% Gemini-2.5-Pro, 53.3% GPT-5.1, 40.0% Claude-Sonnet-4.5), outperforming RL-based approaches that generalize poorly.
stories.why_it_matters: Offers a transferable, query-efficient prompt-injection attacker that challenges current RL-based red teaming and provides high-quality adversarial data for evaluating and training agent defenses.
stories.reason: Automated agentic prompt-injection red teaming addresses prompt-injection attacks and scalable red-team data collection — directly targets core LLM security interests and practical evaluation.

stories.title: The Horizon Gap: Planning, Memory, Execution, Training, and Evaluation for Long-Horizon LLM Agents
stories.summary: The paper defines the horizon gap: LLMs that excel in single-pass reasoning still fail on multi-hour, multi-step tasks, and surveys 1,547 arXiv papers (2024–2026) collected via a systematic seed harvest with a 26.8% bleed filter plus targeted supplementation. It distinguishes long-horizon, long-context, and long-term memory, and organizes the literature into six lifecycle categories (planning, memory, execution, training, evaluation, foundations/safety) crossed with where horizons are carried (within-context, within-task-beyond-context, cross-task-persistent). A recurring finding is that outcome-only signals become uninformative as horizons increase, prompting methods that create denser step-level signals (e.g., process rewards, credit assignment, trajectory diagnostics), and the paper highlights open measurement problems around decomposing model vs. harness capability, correlated bias in process-level signals, and the possibility of a general predictive theory of long-horizon reliability.
stories.why_it_matters: It maps the long-horizon agent landscape, clarifies signal-design pitfalls, and surfaces open measurement issues directly relevant to LLM safety, agent reliability, and long-horizon training/eval design.
stories.reason: Directly targets long-horizon failure modes in LLM agents—survey synthesizes planning, memory, evaluation and training gaps relevant to agentic security and long-context modeling.

stories.title: LabelFusion-TS: Fusing Large Language Models, Transformer Encoders, and Financial Time Series for Monetary-Policy Stance Classification
stories.reason: Multimodal fusion of financial time series with LLMs for stance classification touches the reader's TSFM interest (benchmarks/architectures) and evaluation, though it's a narrow financial NLP application.

stories_overflow.title: HarnessSafe: Evaluating Safety Across Persistent Carriers in Agent Harnesses
stories_overflow.summary: The paper introduces HarnessSafe, a benchmark of 328 executable cases spanning seven persistent-carrier families to assess delayed safety risks in agent harnesses that persist state across tasks and sessions. Each case is defined as a Persistent-Risk Lifecycle that traces attacker influence from entry through cross-carrier persistence to a benign trigger and an observable violation, and a multi-stage, trace-based evaluation measures how far each attack progresses and where it is stopped. Experiments indicate containment is carrier-specific and depends strongly on the harness-model configuration, with both harness and model shaping outcomes and attack success rates failing to capture lifecycle progression patterns.
stories_overflow.why_it_matters: It offers a carrier-aware, trace-based methodology and dataset to dissect how safety risks propagate across memory/tools/skills in agentic systems—complementing coarse success-rate metrics and informing defense design in LLM agents and persistent pipelines.
stories_overflow.reason: Benchmarks delayed safety risks from persistent carriers in agent harnesses; directly targets attack surfaces (memory, tools, skills), evaluation methodology, and end-to-end exploit propagation — highly relevant to LLM security and agentic threat models.

stories_overflow.title: Matryoshka Language Model Suites
stories_overflow.summary: The paper introduces a Matryoshka training framework that nests sub-models of increasing size into one end-to-end trained architecture, reducing total suite parameters and enabling step-wise distillation from the largest to all smaller sub-models. This structure is well-suited for speculative decoding because the draft model is contained within the verifier. A 500M/1.5B/3B suite matches independently trained baselines on benchmarks and perplexities while using 36% less training compute and yielding 14–26% higher speculative decoding throughput, with ablations provided on architectural choices.
stories_overflow.why_it_matters: It offers a practical path to multi-size LLM suites that cut training/inference cost and improve speculative decoding, directly relevant to secure, efficient deployment pipelines and scalable time-series/LLM hybrid stacks.
stories_overflow.reason: Direct audit showing internal harmfulness scores can anti-rank successful jailbreaks—highly relevant to guardrail evaluation, false-positive budgeting, and deployment filtering.

stories_overflow.title: Toward Metacognitive One-Shot Indirect Prompt Injection: Strategy Abstraction Via Outcome-Conditioned Reflection
stories_overflow.summary: The paper introduces SAVOR, a one-shot IPI attack framework that moves adaptation offline via outcome-conditioned reflection over successful and failed trajectories from disjoint training environments, consolidating validated, context-conditioned strategies into a reusable strategy memory. At test time, the frozen memory generates a single payload per unseen target without iterative interaction or feedback, achieving the highest average attack success rate across two benchmarks and three victim models. On Agent Security Bench and the new executable OpenClaw-IPI, SAVOR outperforms the strongest prior attack by 2.5–11.8 points and beats the same injection channel without strategy learning by 23.1 and 28.6 points respectively, with learned memory transferring across defenses.
stories_overflow.why_it_matters: Demonstrates practical one-shot IPI via offline strategy distillation that generalizes across tools, goals, and defenses—relevant for red-teaming LLM agents and for designing defenses that hold under realistic single-interaction constraints.
stories_overflow.reason: One-shot indirect prompt injection (IPI) attacks on tool-using agents via offline strategy distillation directly targets agentic attack surfaces and realistic attacker models—highly relevant to LLM security and red-teaming methodology.

stories_overflow.title: Telemetry and Concealment in Self-Adapting Generative AI: Logging Architecture, Adversarial Model Hiding, and the Limits of Detection
stories_overflow.summary: The paper addresses governance for self-updating generative models by proposing a telemetry architecture that operates in discrete and continuous time, including a Minimal Sufficient Statistic for audits, a Merkle-chain for discrete weight sequences, an Ito-based continuous-time generalization, and KL divergence stopping-time logging. It then formalizes the Model Hiding Problem under adversarial providers and catalogs six attack strategies against the telemetry architecture across discrete and continuous time, providing a countermeasure for each. The result is a dual-regime approach where continuous telemetry narrows but cannot replace periodic invasive audits, aligning with traditional MRM pillars and remaining architecture-agnostic.
stories_overflow.why_it_matters: It offers concrete telemetry and adversarial-resilience mechanisms directly applicable to secure deployment and monitoring of self-adapting LLMs and time-series models where online weight updates break standard validation.
stories_overflow.reason: Directly addresses governance and detection challenges for self-adapting generative models, including telemetry and concealment—highly relevant to security, operational risk, and monitoring of adaptive LLMs.

stories_overflow.title: ElasticBack: Stealthy Conditional Backdoor in LLM-Agent Skills via Coupled Trigger-Rule Optimization
stories_overflow.summary: The paper introduces ElasticBack, a conditional single-skill backdoor for LLM agents that couples a malicious rule R in the skill document with a benign-looking trigger T in user queries, activating only when both appear. It constructs R via semantic-anchored rule injection and then fixes R while evolving T using a stealth-constrained genetic search to optimize attack effectiveness and stealth without modifying model weights. Experiments over three target behaviors (50 skills each) and four agent LLMs show high ASR with near-zero FPR, preserved clean accuracy, cross-model transfer, and evasion of deployment-time defenses, motivating stronger supply-chain defenses for skills.
stories_overflow.why_it_matters: Highlights a practical, weight-free, conditional backdoor vector in the emerging agent skill ecosystem, relevant to securing tool-using LLMs and evaluating defenses against stealthy trigger-rule couplings.
stories_overflow.reason: Presents a stealthy conditional backdoor attack targeting agent skills (supply-chain threat) with low-cost single-skill triggers—highly relevant to LLM agent security, tool/skill poisoning, and defense evaluation.

stories_overflow.title: On Understanding, Identifying, and Mitigating Vulnerabilities in Agentic Large Language Models
stories_overflow.summary: This paper reviews 85 papers (2023–2025) on security of agentic LLMs, selected via a PRISMA 2020 systematic process from 743 records, finding attack work outpaces defenses by 3.9:1. It reports that perception-layer vulnerabilities (prompt injection, jailbreaking, adversarial perturbations) dominate at 66%, while action-layer issues (tool misuse, code injection, sandbox escape) are only 4.7%, with code execution at 3.5% and tool-augmented agents at 12%. The authors propose a four-layer taxonomy (perception, brain, action, interaction) covering 13 vulnerability types, identify seven open problems focused on containment, and argue that weak isolation and architectural coupling let failures propagate across layers.
stories_overflow.why_it_matters: It quantifies where current security work is misaligned with real agentic risk surfaces and offers a layered taxonomy and containment-focused agenda that can guide rigorous evaluations and defenses for tool-using, code-executing LLM agents.
stories_overflow.reason: Systematic review focused on vulnerabilities unique to agentic LLMs (tool use, persistent memory, state changes) directly matches the reader's primary interest in agent attack surfaces and red‑teaming.

stories_overflow.title: Beyond Single-Turn Confidence: Trajectory-Adapted Uncertainty Quantification for LLM Agents
stories_overflow.summary: The paper evaluates whether three families of single-turn UQ methods—white-box action-token probability scorers, black-box resampled-trajectory consistency scorers, and reflexive self-assessment—transfer to multi-turn LLM agent trajectories. Across five LLMs and four multi-turn tool-use datasets from BFCL-v4 and τ^2-bench, they find transfer is useful but uneven: token-probability scores are highly sensitive to cross-turn aggregation, reflexive scores are the strongest low-cost baseline in most settings, and black-box self-consistency is often strongest, particularly trajectory-equivalence and action-set consistency. The results argue for revalidating single-generation UQ at the trajectory level with careful choices of consistency metric, aggregator, and compute budget.
stories_overflow.why_it_matters: Highlights which UQ families and design choices actually work for multi-step agent trajectories, informing security risk estimation and reliability for tool-using and planning LLMs.
stories_overflow.reason: Uncertainty quantification across multi‑turn agent trajectories directly informs evaluation and defenses for LLM agents using tools and stateful workflows — high relevance to agentic security and UQ methodology.

stories_overflow.title: Gradient Immunity: Null-Space Resistance to Malicious Fine-Tuning
stories_overflow.summary: The paper targets the PPOW setting where most weights are trainable but a small safety-critical component is preserved, and proposes a Unidirectional Safety Gate implemented as a Null Space Cubic Layer plus an Inverse Adapter after the final Transformer layer. The cubic layer blocks or suppresses gradients from harmful samples whose hidden states lie within a calibrated protected region (threshold set using defender-held harmful data), while the Inverse Adapter restores the base model’s forward behavior. Across six model–dataset settings, this keeps post-finetuning attack success near pre-release levels under a fixed threshold, maintains high safe-pass on easier settings, and shows a clearer safety–utility trade-off on BeaverTails unsafe samples, indicating release-time representation-space blocking can raise the cost of malicious adaptation without downstream cooperation.
stories_overflow.why_it_matters: Offers a concrete, release-time gradient-blocking mechanism that preserves forward behavior while resisting malicious fine-tuning—relevant to robust alignment under open-weight releases and complementary to gradient/representation-control methods in LLM safety.
stories_overflow.reason: Direct defense proposal against malicious fine-tuning of released weights (PPOW setting) — highly relevant to LLM security, supply-chain attacks, and robustness of deployed models.

stories_overflow.title: Enhancing Anomaly Resilience in Research Networks: A Large-Scale Forecasting Benchmark for Dynamic Security Baselining
stories_overflow.summary: The paper introduces a high-fidelity traffic forecasting framework to create dynamic security baselines for RENs, addressing the challenge that elephant flows resemble volumetric attacks to conventional monitors. Using a 57-day Internet2 dataset (13.7B packets across ten backbone routers), it benchmarks six forecasting model families, including SARIMA and long-sequence architectures (TiDE, PatchTST), over 960 configurations. Results show advanced models—especially TiDE—reduce baseline prediction error by 30–42% (p < 0.001) and that a new anomaly-integration strategy yields a 3.3% robustness gain under noise, improving separation of scientific bursts from anomalies.
stories_overflow.why_it_matters: It provides a statistically validated, large-scale benchmark showing long-sequence LLM-adjacent forecasters (e.g., TiDE/PatchTST) materially improve dynamic baselining for REN security, informing robust anomaly detection under bursty traffic.
stories_overflow.reason: AMS detects safety-training modifications via activation geometry across major model families—highly pertinent to model integrity, detection of fine-tune/backdoor changes and LLM security for deployed models.

stories_overflow.title: When Experience Becomes Instruction: Trajectory Poisoning in Self-Evolving Agent Skill Systems
stories_overflow.summary: The paper introduces PoisonedEvolution, a trajectory-poisoning attack on self-evolving skill (SES) systems that distill agent trajectories into persistent skills, where an attacker with skill-level black-box access contributes bounded evidence to influence skill promotion. It formalizes artifact poisoning as requiring Inclusion, Evolution Attribution, and Realization, identifying Attribution—making target behaviors appear causally useful, recurrent, and generalizable—as the key bottleneck, and demonstrates high success embedding target behaviors across six LLM evolvers in SkillClaw (91.0% SER) and transfer to Trace2Skill (61.5% SER) at 10% attacker support. Controlled studies show three consistent attacker records in a 30-record batch suffice while one is much weaker, and ablations highlight recurring support, causal framing, and domain-aligned encoding as main success factors, framing evidence promotion as a critical security boundary for self-evolving agents.
stories_overflow.why_it_matters: It pinpoints the promotion/attribution step in skill evolution as an attack surface with quantified vulnerability and transferable effects, informing defenses for agentic LLMs and data-driven skill distillation pipelines.
stories_overflow.reason: Robust context-aware segmentation for malicious instructions (IPI) targets detection of embedded prompt injections tailored to a query—highly relevant to defending agents and evaluating instruction-level attacks.

stories_overflow.title: When Do PEFT Adaptations Leak Structure? Measuring Black-Box Structural Bounds in Public-Base Model Services
stories_overflow.summary: The paper introduces VectorHijack-SR, a black-box measurement method that turns paired victim/base residuals into calibrated bounds over PEFT family, layer locality, and coarse rank, using aggregated query-level statistics and a service-disjoint classifier plus a cross-fitted hierarchical rejector to test LoRA-manifold membership. Empirically, family leakage exceeds chance across multiple backbones/tasks, rank inference varies by task, the rejector attains AUROC 0.804 and high known-set accuracy but struggles with structurally close DoRA/LoRA+head, and exact-version linkage on held-out LoRA-r64 services reaches AUC 0.940. Despite measurable structural leakage, experiments show a visibility–exploitability gap: two-stage recovery offers no fair-budget query savings, posterior-selected PEFT underperforms distill-then-convert PEFT, and free-running generation remains near chance.
stories_overflow.why_it_matters: It provides concrete, black-box evidence and metrics for structural leakage from PEFTed services with known bases, informing red-team audits, model fingerprinting, and security evaluations of adapter deployment choices.
stories_overflow.reason: Directly studies information leakage from PEFT adapters in public-base services — highly relevant to model extraction, PIi leakage, and red-team measurement for LLM security.

stories_overflow.title: Towards a Risk Assessment of Malicious Skill Files in Coding Agents
stories_overflow.summary: The paper studies the attack surface introduced by agent skill folders in autonomous coding agents and presents an adversarial skill-synthesis method that converts 471 real shell commands into 2,826 benign-looking skills mapped to 11 ATT&CK tactics using six LLMs. It introduces a reproducible evaluation pipeline with stratification, evidence anchoring, refusal veto, and a deterministic declared-intent override, using a three-judge LLM panel validated against a blind human gold standard (κ=0.85). In large-scale tests (5,629 runs), Gemini CLI was exploited in 95.5–96.1% and Qwen Code in 71.6–74.0% of runs with only 1.99% explicit safety recognition, and code/dataset are released at https://github.com/awsm-research/AgentJailbreak.
stories_overflow.why_it_matters: Provides a validated benchmark, eval pipeline, and high-base-rate exploitation evidence for skill-file attacks in coding agents—directly relevant to LLM security evals and agentic deployment risk.
stories_overflow.reason: Demonstrates pipeline attack surface in coding agents by hiding malicious shell commands in natural-language skill files — directly applicable to agentic-system attack vectors and red-teaming.

stories_overflow.title: A Six-Dimensional Taxonomy of Post-Training Adaptation Techniques with Applications in AI Governance
stories_overflow.summary: This survey synthesizes post-training adaptation techniques—spanning retraining, fine-tuning, parameter-efficient adaptation, alignment, RAG, model editing, unlearning, calibration, and multimodal instruction tuning—and introduces a six-dimensional taxonomy by mechanism, goal, data requirement, persistence, structural scope, and model type. It clarifies conflated terms (e.g., fine-tuning vs. RAG vs. prompting), traces the evolution of adaptation across model eras, and maps relationships such as inheritance, supersession, hybridization, and layered deployment stacks. The work presents a vocabulary to support technical documentation, change tracking, and governance analysis, and highlights open challenges in evaluation, reproducibility, persistent inference-time adaptation, unlearning, multimodal adaptation, and governance-aware workflows.
stories_overflow.why_it_matters: Provides a governance-aligned taxonomy that can standardize how LLM security adaptations (e.g., alignment, unlearning, RAG) are described, compared, and tracked across deployment stacks, aiding reproducible evaluation and auditability.
stories_overflow.reason: Presents a timestep-conditioned transformer for global weather forecasting addressing timestep choice trade-offs—directly relevant to TSFM pretraining/objectives and long-horizon forecasting design.

stories_overflow.title: LoRAScan: Detecting Backdoor Prompts in Low-Rank Adapters for Large Language Models via Down-Projection Activation Spikes
stories_overflow.summary: The paper introduces LoRAScan, an adapter-aware defense that detects and rejects trigger-bearing inputs for potentially backdoored LoRA adapters at inference time without modifying adapter parameters. It exploits the observation that about 5% of LoRA insertion sites exhibit stable activations on clean inputs but show concentrated spikes in down-projection activations when a trigger is present; these sites are identified pre-deployment and monitored online. On standard LLM backdoor benchmarks, LoRAScan rejects approximately 98.49 of malicious inputs with a small error rate on clean inputs, outperforming existing defenses across diverse settings.
stories_overflow.why_it_matters: It offers a practical, deployment-compatible defense for LoRA-based supply-chain backdoors by leveraging activation signatures rather than adapter merging or retraining, aligning with current interests in robust LLM fine-tuning security.
stories_overflow.reason: LoRAScan targets backdoored LoRA adapters—a direct supply-chain threat to LLM security (adapter-level backdoors) and practical detection method relevant to applied defenses.

stories_overflow.title: Deployable Per-Instance Multi-Layer Activation Steering for Large Language Models
stories_overflow.summary: The paper shows that in activation steering, the optimal injection layers vary per input, with per-instance multi-layer selection outperforming any fixed global layer set across six binary persona traits on two 8B models. A greedy layer-ranking rule based on single-layer marginal effects nearly matches a per-instance oracle but requires gold labels, so the authors train a prompt-only predictor to mimic it and propose a deployable recipe: a prompt-based per-instance layer ranker, a classifier to infer steering direction, and an adaptive gate that limits layers by short steered passes. This deployable approach recovers most of the oracle’s gains, avoids dropping below unsteered baselines on average, reduces fluency collapse relative to strong global selection, and is supported by a mechanistic account emphasizing direction over magnitude that explains misdirection flips, collapse from over-steering, and unsteerable ceilings.
stories_overflow.why_it_matters: It operationalizes per-instance, label-free activation steering with adaptive multi-layer control, offering a practical path to safer, targeted behavior edits without sacrificing fluency—relevant to red-teaming defenses and controllable generation, and conceptually aligned with direction-based causal hypotheses familiar in interpretability.
stories_overflow.reason: Per-instance multi-layer activation steering directly targets editing/model control at inference time—relevant to attack/defense surfaces, deployment, and efficient selective interventions for LLM security and agent behavior.

stories_overflow.title: Activation Probes Surface Code-Security Signals that the Model's Output Misses
stories_overflow.summary: The authors study whether linear probes on open-weight reviewer models’ activations reveal code-security signals that the same models’ outputs miss. Trained on paired vulnerable/fixed Python functions and evaluated zero-shot on real disclosed vulns (including unseen weakness types) across five models, a single probe per model ranks the vulnerable version above its fix in 61–67% of single-function-fix cases, exceeding chance and the model’s own prompted YES/NO logit-based decisions under all prompts tested. Written verdicts (including CoT) typically fail to distinguish vulnerable from fixed code, suggesting activations encode a security signal not surfaced by prompting.
stories_overflow.why_it_matters: It shows latent security-relevant information in LLM activations can be extracted with simple probes even when model outputs fail, informing red-teaming, interpretability, and toolstack design for secure code generation with closed-weight agents + open-weight reviewers.
stories_overflow.reason: Probing activations to surface vulnerabilities that outputs miss offers an interpretable detection avenue for code-security in generated artifacts—valuable for scalable review and red-team tooling.

stories_overflow.title: DiffSafeMerge: Mitigating Backdoor Inheritance in Diffusion Model Merging
stories_overflow.summary: The paper highlights that merging diffusion checkpoints can inherit dormant backdoors from compromised public sources while maintaining normal-looking generations, and mitigating this is hard without knowing the attacker specifics or sacrificing quality. It proposes DiffSafeMerge, which uses a small unlabeled clean set and fixed attack-agnostic stress probes to score source blocks, attenuate suspicious contributions toward a trusted reference, and choose attenuation under a clean denoising-loss budget. Evaluated across four attacks, two datasets, and 21 targets, DSM preserves zero worst-target ASR where intended merging already had it, eliminates remaining matches over three seeds even when baseline ASR was 48–100%, and among methods with zero worst-target ASR on both datasets achieves the lowest case-averaged FID in the seed-0 comparison.
stories_overflow.why_it_matters: Backdoor-safe merging for diffusion checkpoints parallels secure model composition in LLMs and offers a practical, attack-agnostic mitigation strategy that balances safety with generative quality.
stories_overflow.reason: Telemetry and concealment for self-adapting generative AI addresses governance and detection limits for models that modify themselves in production—important for model-risk management, attack concealment, and detection strategies.

stories_overflow.title: SkillsMetric: Mapping the Detection Boundary of Static Analysis for Malicious Agent Skills
stories_overflow.summary: This work introduces SkillsMetric, a five-stage static analysis framework that scores LLM agent skills across pattern density, statistical anomaly, dataflow taint, import anomaly, and capability mismatch. Using an adversarial dataset of 2,266 skills covering 16 attack types and the SkillMD-138K corpus, it reports AUC 0.93 and 5-fold CV F1 73.4%±0.5%, with 93% detection for data exfiltration and steganographic payloads. It also exposes blind spots—0% detection for host destruction via common shell commands and 42% for prompt injection—arguing static analysis alone is insufficient and should be paired with semantic review in defense-in-depth.
stories_overflow.why_it_matters: Directly maps the detection boundary of static analysis for agent skills, highlighting failure modes (e.g., prompt injection, host destruction) that inform red-teaming, hybrid detection pipelines, and security benchmarks for LLM agents.
stories_overflow.reason: Static analysis scoring of agent 'skills' maps to supply-chain and capability-based attack surfaces for LLM agents and helps red-teaming/defense of tool-augmented systems.

stories_overflow.title: Persistent Semantic Entities in Tool-Augmented LLM Systems
stories_overflow.summary: The paper formalizes Persistent Semantic Entities (PSEs) in tool-augmented LLM agents—defined by name binding, event triggering, and cross-boundary propagation—and shows all 24 tested models are susceptible, with name binding necessary and dominant (0% without it). Persistence depends on contamination type: preference contamination persists undegraded (100% at t=10), instruction contamination persists where adopted, persona injection partially decays (90%→10%), and factual injection varies by model (self-corrected on Llama-3.1-8B and GPT-4o-mini but not on Qwen2.5-coder variants). Context-isolated self-verification reduces contamination by 20–79% (median 36.5%) versus keyword detectors with systematic false positives, and contamination compounds 1.9× through a four-stage agent pipeline (40%→75%), with preference/instruction contamination highlighted as a concerning attack surface.
stories_overflow.why_it_matters: Directly informs red-teaming and defenses for agentic LLMs by identifying name-binding-driven, cross-session contamination modes that persist, evade naive monitoring, and amplify in pipelines.
stories_overflow.reason: Inference-time guard that routes capabilities to avoid reasoning-centric jailbreaks targets a new, practical jailbreak class and proposes model-agnostic mitigations relevant for deployment.

stories_overflow.title: Rethinking Self-Evolving Agents: Do We Still Need Prescribed Optimization Pipelines?
stories_overflow.summary: The paper introduces Open-Ended Optimization (OEO), which fixes objective, interactions, budget, data boundary, and evaluation while letting a frontier model compose the optimization process online, contrasting it with two prescribed pipelines: SkillOpt and GEPA. In 14 head-to-head tests over 8 benchmark–target-model settings, GPT-5.5–driven OEO wins 12, ties 1, and narrowly loses 1 (by 0.21 pp) while using a median 34.3% of SkillOpt’s interaction-token budget; a one-shot zero-interaction control indicates gains aren’t from a single rewrite. However, delegation is capability-bound: SkillOpt beats OEO with a medium optimizer, a weak optimizer fails under OEO’s interface, and trajectory analysis shows prescription shapes optimization trajectories more than final behavior, framing prescribed pipelines as capability-dependent scaffolding.
stories_overflow.why_it_matters: Challenges assumptions about fixed self-improvement pipelines by showing frontier-model-driven open-ended optimization can outperform prescribed schemes under tight budgets, clarifying capability thresholds and offering a new design point for secure, efficient LLM self-improvement workflows.
stories_overflow.reason: Examines self-evolving agents and whether prescribed optimization pipelines remain necessary when using frontier models as optimizers—important for agent safety, emergent optimization behaviors, and red-teaming agentic pipelines.

stories_overflow.title: An Empirical Study of Output-to-Input Loops for Black-Box Backdoor Detection in Fine-Tuned Open-Weight LLMs
stories_overflow.summary: The paper proposes self-feeding, a black-box test that recursively feeds a model’s outputs back as inputs to drift toward fine-tuning data, enabling backdoor discovery without training data, clean baselines, or trigger knowledge. Evaluated on six open-weight LLMs (3B–15B) with eleven backdoor categories and twenty prompts over up to ten steps, self-feeding detects backdoors in five models with 92.0% pooled precision, while a same-prompt baseline succeeds on only one of 120 prompt-model pairs; some prompts (jokes, arithmetic, coffee recipes) reach triggers in a few steps. Despite low per-prompt recall (19.2%), multi-prompt use raises model-level detection, though one model never triggers and there are two false positives; truncating to four steps preserves 100% model-level precision and cuts queries by 60%.
stories_overflow.why_it_matters: Offers a cheap, black-box, text-only stress test that surfaces fine-tune data modes (including backdoors) via output-to-input loops, complementing existing evals for open-weight LLMs and informing detection strategies for security-focused and time-series-style iterative generation analyses.
stories_overflow.reason: Black‑box self‑feeding method for detecting backdoors in fine‑tuned open LLMs is directly applicable to model vetting, backdoor detection, and practical security checks for deployed models.

stories_overflow.title: Generating Attacks for LLMs with GFlowNets
stories_overflow.summary: The work proposes an automated, human-independent red teaming framework that trains an attacker LLM via GFlowNets to probe a specified victim LLM and yield a quantitative robustness score. It addresses limitations of manual expert red teaming and automated methods tied to fixed datasets by enabling adaptive, creative attack generation. The approach targets generating more effective English adversarial inputs than existing benchmarks and, uniquely, introduces Turkish-language attack generation.
stories_overflow.why_it_matters: It explores GFlowNets for adaptive attack synthesis against LLMs, offering a path beyond fixed corpora and extending multilingual red teaming—a relevant direction for security evaluation and scalable adversarial data generation.
stories_overflow.reason: Uses GFlowNets to autogenerate adversarial attacks for LLM red‑teaming — directly relevant to scalable red‑teaming and attack generation for LLM security.

stories_overflow.title: Personalized Federated Sparse Adaptation of Time-Series Foundation Models
stories_overflow.summary: The paper proposes a personalized federated sparse adaptation framework for TSFMs in building energy forecasting, using a heterogeneous temporal MoE adapter placed after the pretrained representation and a sequence-level router that assigns each 168-hour window to top-k experts specialized for distinct temporal structures. It evaluates global FL, local training, and personalized FL variants with globally shared vs client-private expert banks across 50 buildings and three TSFM backbones. Results show personalization consistently outperforms Global FL-MoE and Local MoE, the best sparse-adaptation strategy depends on backbone and metric, and routing reveals client-level expert specialization, expert concentration, and near-uniform routing across backbones, implying adaptation should be client- and backbone-aware.
stories_overflow.why_it_matters: Combines federated personalization with sparse MoE routing for TSFMs under non-IID meter data, offering actionable design signals (client-/backbone-aware adapters) relevant to secure on-device adaptation and privacy-preserving deployment.
stories_overflow.reason: Federated personalization for TS foundation models directly matches the reader's primary interest in TSFMs and on-device/private data adaptation; MoE adapter and sparse adaptation are relevant to architecture and efficient adaptation.

stories_overflow.title: Do All LLMs Know When They're Being Harmful? A Reproducibility Study of Latent-Space Safety Probes Across Model Families
stories_overflow.summary: This study reproduces Khatri et al.’s pipeline for training lightweight MLP probes on final-layer activations to detect harmful prompts, matching the original LLaMA-3.1-8B results within 0.37 F1 points (0.2 on BeaverTails). It extends the evaluation across Gemma-4-E4B, Mistral-7B-v0.3, and Qwen2-7B on WildJailbreak, BeaverTails, and AEGIS 2.0, finding F1 within about one point of the LLaMA-3.1-8B values using the same probe architecture. It also assesses nondeterminism by varying seeds and reports that final token latent vectors were invariant to seed across architectures.
stories_overflow.why_it_matters: Suggests simple latent-space probes generalize across model families with stable activations, informing scalable, low-overhead safety detection for LLMs and complementing guardrail strategies.
stories_overflow.reason: Reproducibility of latent safety probes across model families evaluates a lightweight detection approach that could scale as a defense or monitoring tool for harmful prompt detection.

stories_overflow.title: Who Verifies the Benchmark? Decentralizing Trust in Large Language Model Evaluation
stories_overflow.summary: The paper argues that LLM evaluation lacks verifiability and is vulnerable to unverified vendor claims and LLM-judge identity bias, with real-world consequences highlighted by the January 27, 2025 market panic. Using seven verifier models, it measures how disclosing the source model identity shifts scores across 58 factual, reasoning, political, and preference tasks, finding minimal effects on factual items, moderate effects on stress-reasoning, and large effects on geopolitically sensitive topics, with examples including GLM 5.1 (+7.00, p=0.0249) and Llama 3.3 70B (+1.56, p=0.00). It proposes a blockchain-based commit–reveal protocol with Autonomous Economic Agents to create an on-chain, tamper-evident audit trail that separates blind evaluation from post-hoc claims and eases verification for researchers and leaderboard operators.
stories_overflow.why_it_matters: Directly relevant to LLM security and evaluation: quantifies identity-aware judge bias across sensitive tasks and offers a verifiable, decentralized commit–reveal protocol that could harden benchmark integrity and leaderboards.
stories_overflow.reason: Model editing for secure code generation evaluates model-level hardening methods versus inference-time approaches — relevant to reducing malicious or vulnerable generations in deployed LLMs.

stories_overflow.title: verdi: retrieval is not transfer for continual world model optimization
stories_overflow.summary: The paper argues that retrieval is not transfer in optimizing pretrained world models: strategies validated on one model are only hypotheses for another and require target-side experimental validation. It introduces VERDI, a continual evidence-licensed optimization framework that builds Optimization Fingerprints via shared inference-time probes, retrieves prior strategies as ranked hypotheses, and validates them with a frozen target-side verifier while evolving probes when contradictions arise. Experiments on Ctrl-World, Cosmos, and RoboCoin report reduced search (68%), GPU cost (69%), negative transfer (0.34→0.06), and 83% sign accuracy in predicting transfer outcomes.
stories_overflow.why_it_matters: Offers a principled, verifier-gated alternative to recipe-style transfer for model optimization, aligning with secure/evidence-based LLM and time-series/world-model tuning where negative transfer and brittle heuristics are major pain points.
stories_overflow.reason: Argues that retrieved strategies don't directly transfer for optimizing world models and proposes safeguarding transfer—relevant to continual optimization of foundation world/time-series models and efficient automated optimization agents.

stories_overflow.title: RouteGuard: Certifying Routing Gain in LLM Multi-Agent Systems When Complementarity Is Not Enough
stories_overflow.summary: The paper shows that common assumptions for multi-agent LLM routing—optimizing gate AUC and relying on advisor complementarity—do not determine deployable gain, and introduces RouteGuard to certify routing benefit. It decomposes gain as G = πΔ_E, identifies a conditional-regret functional Φ as the governing quantity (not AUC), provides a finite-sample certification bracket with a matching Le Cam lower bound that is constant-sharp over the fixed-activity class, and observes a robustness phase transition. Experiments on RouterBench and OpenRCA demonstrate RouteGuard acting as a guardrail, certifying gain only under prompt-level sampling (not workload-cluster resampling) on RouterBench and refusing to certify on OpenRCA due to advisor redundancy, with pre-registered semi-synthetic controls confirming calibration thresholds.
stories_overflow.why_it_matters: It offers a principled, sample-sensitive certification of routing gain that can prevent illusory improvements in LLM multi-agent systems and aligns evaluation with deployment risk.
stories_overflow.reason: Analyzes routing certification in LLM multi-advisor systems and provides finite-sample guarantees for when routing yields deployable gain—relevant to safe agent composition, evaluation metrics beyond AUC, and deployment-risk assessment.

stories_overflow.title: Measure, Don't Optimize: Forecasting Recovery in LLM Unlearning
stories_overflow.summary: The paper introduces J-Access, an inference-time audit that projects intermediate representations into vocabulary space to measure how often target concepts remain accessible along the output pathway, hypothesizing that residual accessibility predicts recovery susceptibility. Auditing 398 public unlearned models across eight methods, they find most retain accessibility above a retain-only gold level, pre-attack accessibility predicts recovery speed and extent at the model level (but not per-fact), and directly minimizing J-Access causes the model to hide knowledge from the audit while increasing post-attack recovery. They conclude J-Access is useful as a model-level diagnostic for residual susceptibility and caution against turning internal audits into optimization targets without validation.
stories_overflow.why_it_matters: Offers an actionable, model-level risk signal for unlearning robustness and a clear warning about Goodharting internal audits—relevant for designing secure unlearning and audit pipelines in LLMs.
stories_overflow.reason: Investigates latent recovery after LLM unlearning with an audit (J‑Access) — important for data‑removal/extraction risk monitoring and evaluation methodology.

stories_overflow.title: HarnessOpt-Bench: Evaluating LLMs at Harness Optimization
stories_overflow.summary: The paper introduces HarnessOpt-Bench, a benchmark for end-to-end harness optimization where an LLM optimizer iteratively edits a target agent’s harness under expensive, stochastic evaluation with a fixed budget, using only graded feedback and without access to a held-out test partition. A trusted execution environment enforces evaluation boundaries, meters resource use, and preserves candidate versions for audit, and performance is measured by normalized gain over the seed harness. Evaluating five frontier LLMs across four tasks and 111 runs, the authors find optimizer models differentiate more than coding harnesses, native harnesses aren’t consistently superior, and gains vary substantially by task and seed regime, establishing harness optimization as a measurable and discriminative capability with room for improvement.
stories_overflow.why_it_matters: It provides a rigorous, auditable setup to compare LLMs’ agentic self-improvement under realistic noisy/expensive evals—relevant for secure agent orchestration and optimizing time-series/tool-using pipelines.
stories_overflow.reason: Benchmark for optimizing agent harnesses is directly relevant to LLM agent security (attack surface via prompts/tools/orchestration) and offers an evaluation protocol useful for red-teaming and robust harness design.

stories_overflow.title: DBLAST: Dependent Block Drafting for Stochastic Speculative Decoding
stories_overflow.summary: The paper analyzes speculative decoding with block/diffusion drafters and shows that assuming conditional independence across drafted positions breaks down under non-greedy, higher-entropy target sampling, reducing accepted draft length. It introduces DBLAST, a dependent block drafter using a low-rank latent mixture over token positions plus an acceptance-oriented objective that optimizes expected verified length. Experiments on Qwen3-4B/8B across GSM8K, MT-Bench, HumanEval, and creative-writing benchmarks report consistent gains in accepted length over independent block sampling, particularly at higher entropy.
stories_overflow.why_it_matters: It targets stochastic decoding efficiency—key for secure, diverse sampling and alignment workflows—by improving acceptance rates under high-entropy regimes, informing both LLM safety pipelines and efficient inference design.
stories_overflow.reason: Speculative decoding for stochastic drafts impacts efficient inference for agents and could change threat surface of model outputs when combined with stochasticity — relevant to scalable red-teaming and secure deployment.

stories_overflow.title: EdgeXpert: An Edge Device for Memory-Efficient LLM Inference with Mixture-of-Experts and Speculative Decoding
stories_overflow.summary: EdgeXpert is a software-hardware co-designed LLM accelerator targeting the EMA bottleneck in FFN layers for on-device inference, combining speculative decoding with MoE despite their typical incompatibility. In prefill, it uses prompt-wise expert reuse by selecting important tokens via a lightweight encoder to build a shared expert set and routes less important tokens with a reduced expert budget to cut expert EMA; in decode, depth-aware expert coalescing loads only salient channels across same-depth speculative candidates and applies computational calibration to maintain accuracy without extra memory access. Implemented in Samsung 28nm at 800 MHz, EdgeXpert reports up to 56.3% latency and 44.1% energy reductions versus prior work while maintaining near-baseline accuracy.
stories_overflow.why_it_matters: It offers a practical path to marry MoE with speculative decoding for memory-bound edge inference, yielding sizable latency/energy gains relevant to secure, private on-device LLM deployment and efficient time-sensitive workloads.
stories_overflow.reason: Skill Entropy offers a quantitative measure and training signal for cross-skill long-horizon reasoning, useful for designing and evaluating agents and long-horizon benchmarks relevant to TSFM-style sequence tasks.

stories_overflow.title: Trident : How to Break Deep Reinforcement Learning Cyber Defenses (Agentic)
stories_overflow.summary: The paper introduces Trident, an agentic LLM red-teaming framework for evaluating DRL-based cyber defenses, consisting of a dynamic benchmark across CybORG CAGE 4 and CyberWheel, a dataset of 13k+ red-blue trajectories for RLVR, and a Code-as-Policy RLVR architecture. Trident reframes red-agent training as a contextual bandit using a Log Summarizer–Planner–Coder pipeline, where a trainable Planner produces complete attack strategies from compressed logs and a frozen Coder turns them into executable Python policies against live DRL defenders. Empirically, a single 7B planner substantially degrades blue-agent performance (average 522% reduction vs. static red baselines) and uncovers emergent behaviors like decoy avoidance and adaptive state prioritization that static heuristics miss.
stories_overflow.why_it_matters: It demonstrates an RLVR-driven, code-generating agent that reliably breaks DRL cyber defenses and provides a benchmark/dataset, directly informing LLM security evaluation and agent robustness research.
stories_overflow.reason: Provides trajectory-level certification methods for modular LLM-based security agents, addressing guarantees and calibration across multi-stage pipelines — useful for safety evaluation of agentic security systems.

stories_overflow.title: Align-RAG: Alignment Is All You Need for TSFM In-Context Learning
stories_overflow.summary: The paper introduces Align-RAG, a training-free method that applies closed-form amplitude rescaling and integer-lag phase alignment to retrieved past–future windows before feeding them to a frozen TSFM. On a frozen Chronos-Bolt, it outperforms a state-of-the-art trained retrieval adapter across seven benchmark datasets (average −3.75% MSE), and it also improves zero-shot MSE by 2.5%–13.7% on four additional frozen TSFMs without per-backbone tuning. Analysis shows aligned demonstrations induce prediction shifts in frozen backbones that track a closed-form ridge predictor on the same pairs, with a future-shuffle control ruling out futures-averaging, suggesting frozen TSFMs already support dynamic in-context use of retrievals.
stories_overflow.why_it_matters: It challenges the need for learned fusion in RAG for forecasting by showing closed-form alignment on frozen backbones yields SOTA gains and ridge-like in-context adaptation, a strong baseline relevant to LLM alignment and retrieval studies.
stories_overflow.reason: DASH improves on-policy self-distillation for reasoning models with temporally-adaptive supervision horizons — relevant to improving RL-style fine-tuning and evaluation of reasoning/judging behavior and scalable red-teaming.

stories_overflow.title: The Label Defines the Timescale: Trait-State Limits of Temporal-Aggregate Learning
stories_overflow.summary: The paper analyzes labels of temporal aggregates Θ_{g,T} built from a latent Gaussian process with a stable trait and correlated state, using an exact protocol-conditioned Bayes-risk identity. It shows label variance splits into an O(1) trait and O(T^{-1}) state component, derives task-dependent effective temporal spans (means tied to ordinary correlation time; occupation times to higher-order spectra), and proves state-driven occupation-label variance peaks at trait-threshold with window efficiency decaying slowly away from it. With a fixed segment budget, risks and simulations show repeated co-temporal segments saturate quickly while temporally dispersed observations keep improving state explainability; trait ceilings come from test-retest quantities, whereas state ceilings need short-lag calibration, implying observed limits can be protocol-driven rather than architectural.
stories_overflow.why_it_matters: Clarifies when snapshot protocols fundamentally cap aggregate-label predictability and how to design observation schedules to separate architectural limits from acquisition ceilings—directly relevant to security evals of LLM temporal tasks and to designing time series foundation model benchmarks.
stories_overflow.reason: Theoretical limits on temporal-aggregate labels and protocol ceilings are relevant to time-series benchmark design and evaluation of TS foundation models and could inform realistic evaluation ceilings.

stories_overflow.title: FutureBridge: Token Selection Beyond Local Preference in Collaborative Decoding
stories_overflow.summary: FutureBridge proposes a token reranking scheme for LLM–SLM collaborative decoding that prioritizes tokens enabling the SLM’s subsequent reasoning rather than the LLM’s local preference. Training uses an answer-verified LLM trajectory to fix a shared future, while a frozen SLM assigns counterfactual scores to candidate tokens under this common context to supervise a lightweight reranker observing only the current state and token. At inference, the LLM only expands the candidate pool and the reranker selects a single token before handing generation back to the SLM without appending any future suffix, yielding a 35.1% relative Math Avg. improvement for Qwen3-1.7B across five math reasoning benchmarks over greedy decoding.
stories_overflow.why_it_matters: It reframes collaboration as SLM-aware token selection, offering a practical path to safer, stronger small-model reasoning with minimal LLM involvement—relevant to alignment, tool-use gating, and cost/security tradeoffs in cooperative decoding.
stories_overflow.reason: FutureBridge proposes collaborative decoding between LLM and smaller models to improve SLM reasoning—relevant for efficient red-teaming, agent pipelines, and attack/defense strategies where token choice affects downstream agent behavior.

stories_overflow.title: MemWM: Memory-Augmented Text-Based World Model
stories_overflow.summary: MemWM is a memory-augmented text world model that conditions next-state imagination on a curated memory bank of transition rules, state caches, and hard-to-predict facts. It introduces Structured State Fidelity (SSF) to evaluate factual state preservation and shows that memory-augmented training improves SSF by up to 206.3% over SFT. In planning, they freeze the policy and supply policy-side world skill via retrieved task-level skills and step-wise corrective guidance, yielding up to a 65.4% relative success gain across ALFWorld, WebShop, and ScienceWorld, with sensitivity analyses showing benefits across memory and action budgets.
stories_overflow.why_it_matters: Targets a key failure mode in text-based world models—systematic state-transition errors—using retrieval-style memory that cleanly composes with frozen policies, relevant to secure planning and robust long-horizon reasoning.
stories_overflow.reason: Memory-augmented world model aims to preserve factual state across imagined transitions — important for agent reliability and potential attack surfaces (memory corruption), though not explicitly about security.

stories_overflow.title: Measuring the Wrong Thing: Internal Harmfulness Scores Anti-Rank Successful Jailbreaks
stories_overflow.summary: The paper shows that internal safety scores, validated on harmful-intent separation pre-generation, do not predict jailbreak success and can misallocate false positives toward attacks that would have failed. To address prompt-dependent measurement locations, it introduces Active Attention Probing to provide a fixed, content-independent coordinate and evaluates paired plain vs. wrapped prompts with real target-model completions. On Llama, wrapping increases harmful generations from 0.05 to 0.27 while harmful-intent AUROC drops from 0.936 to 0.803, and for wrapped harmful prompts the outcome AUROC is 0.220, with the reversal reproduced across models, attack families, judges, and alternative channels, and with distribution shift harming calibration/threshold transfer before ranking.
stories_overflow.why_it_matters: It challenges the common practice of using pre-generation intent scores as proxies for attack success and offers a measurement fix (AAP) with evidence of anti-correlation under wrapping, directly informing eval design and filter tuning for jailbreak defense.
stories_overflow.reason: Automated discovery and causal verification of spurious shortcuts in text classifiers is relevant to evaluation robustness and dataset contamination/shortcut mitigation.

stories_overflow.title: Tevatron-Elastic: A Unified Abstraction for Training Elastic Retrievers and Rerankers
stories_overflow.summary: Tevatron-Elastic introduces a unified abstraction that encapsulates three orthogonal elasticity axes for IR models—fewer layers, upper-layer token pruning, and shorter embeddings—so a single checkpoint supports multiple runtime sizes selected via a schedule. The abstraction applies uniformly to retrievers and rerankers, encoder and decoder backbones via HF interfaces, subsuming prior methods like Matryoshka embeddings, early exit, 2D Matryoshka (e.g., Starbucks), and layerwise token compression, and also enables Matryoshka LTC for jointly training multiple token-compression ratios in one retriever. Empirically, across 20 checkpoints, three backbones, and two tasks, they report smooth quality curves, near-single-size training cost, and controlled wallclock speedups, releasing the framework and checkpoints for elastic retrieval systems.
stories_overflow.why_it_matters: A clean, composable interface for multi-axis elasticity in retrievers/rerankers simplifies deployment-time cost/quality trade-offs and unifies techniques ML security and systems folks already use (early exit, Matryoshka, token compression) under one training/checkpoint regime.
stories_overflow.reason: Elastic retrievers/rerankers address scalable retrieval tradeoffs and dynamic model-size/runtime adaptation—useful for efficient RAG/agent pipelines and evaluation of retrieval components in security workflows.

stories_overflow.title: Diversity Matters: Distributional Feature Coverage Sample Selection for Data-Efficient Backdoor Attacks
stories_overflow.summary: The paper introduces DFCS, a training-free, trigger-agnostic sample selection method that clusters pretrained features into one region per poisoning slot and picks centroid-nearest samples to avoid redundant poisons. A local first-order analysis links this allocation to feature-coverage and representative-mass terms. On CIFAR-10, Tiny-ImageNet, and Imagenette with BadNets and Blended attacks, DFCS achieves the highest mean ASR among seven selectors in all six settings, averaging 96.30% and surpassing the strongest comparator by 4.60 points on average while maintaining clean accuracy.
stories_overflow.why_it_matters: It highlights a simple, training-free selection principle that boosts low-budget dirty-label backdoor potency, informing both attack design and defenses that rely on data diversity and feature coverage.
stories_overflow.reason: Data-efficient backdoor attack selection is directly relevant to poisoning threats against models and informs attack surface/defense design, though not LLM-specific and focused on vision-style feature clustering.

stories_overflow.title: Capability-Routed Guard: Defending Large Reasoning Models Against Reasoning-Centric Jailbreaks
stories_overflow.summary: The paper introduces Capability-Routed Guard (CRG), a model-agnostic, inference-time guardrail for closed-source LRMs that reframes prompt defense as capability routing by constructing a trusted representation of authorized task, active context, safety evidence, and capability-transfer risk. CRG supports route-specific execution to block high-risk requests, constrain ambiguous ones, and forward low-risk requests via trusted active context, then applies TraceCheck for consistency with the authorized task and uses a restricted fallback to preserve utility for low-risk benign prompts. Experiments show CRG mitigates diverse reasoning-centric jailbreaks while preserving benign utility and avoiding over-refusals, with component analyses indicating complementary benefits and the importance of coordinated defenses for securing LRMs.
stories_overflow.why_it_matters: Directly targets reasoning-centric jailbreaks in LRMs with a practical, model-agnostic routing + verification pipeline that can be layered onto closed-source systems without weights or trace access.
stories_overflow.reason: Discussion of verification, contamination, and LLM-as-judge reliability informs benchmark trust and evaluation methods, important context for honest security/benchmarking practices.

stories_overflow.title: DreamGuard: Efficient Runtime Guardrail for LLM Agents via Risk-Aware World Model
stories_overflow.summary: DreamGuard is a proactive runtime guardrail for LLM agents that uses a risk-aware world model to track a compact recurrent latent state over trajectories and forecast future latent states. items.title: BASIS: Breach-Aware Selective Prompt Injection Shielding with Prefill Attention Probes
items.summary: The paper addresses over-refusal in prompt-injection defenses by noting that aligned models with robust instructions can withstand many injections, so blanket detection-and-refuse strategies are suboptimal. It proposes BASIS, which uses Attention Competition Ratio features to train two sparse linear probes—an existence probe and a breach probe—that operate in a cascaded, no-extra-inference gating pipeline to detect injections, predict per-sample breaches, and assess instruction robustness. Experiments on four tasks and six open-source LLMs report near-perfect injection detection with substantially reduced over-refusal on safe attack samples, particularly when using robust instruction templates.

items.title: Measuring Semantic Abstractness of SAE Features via Nonlocality
items.summary: The paper introduces Feature Nonlocality (FNL), defined as the entropy of the normalized per-position influence on an SAE feature’s activation, as a metric for semantic abstractness. FNL correlates with LLM-based proxy metrics and distinguishes contextual reasoning features from token-driven ones, assigning higher FNL to the contextual feature in 73–84% of mixed pairs. Applications include auditing jailbreak-mitigation features (finding many are low-FNL positional features) and showing that steering high-FNL features can boost MATH-500 accuracy by 4.6 points in DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B, outperforming low-FNL steering though gains are model-specific.
items.why_it_matters: Offers an LLM-independent, label-free criterion to identify genuinely abstract SAE features, informing safer jailbreak defenses and more effective feature steering for reasoning tasks.

items.title: HarnessSafe: Evaluating Safety Across Persistent Carriers in Agent Harnesses
items.summary: The paper introduces HarnessSafe, a benchmark of 328 executable cases spanning seven persistent-carrier families to assess delayed safety risks in agent harnesses that persist state across tasks and sessions. Each case is defined as a Persistent-Risk Lifecycle that traces attacker influence from entry through cross-carrier persistence to a benign trigger and an observable violation, and a multi-stage, trace-based evaluation measures how far each attack progresses and where it is stopped. Experiments indicate containment is carrier-specific and depends strongly on the harness-model configuration, with both harness and model shaping outcomes and attack success rates failing to capture lifecycle progression patterns.

items.reason: Benchmarks delayed safety risks from persistent carriers in agent harnesses; directly targets attack surfaces (memory, tools, skills), evaluation methodology, and end-to-end exploit propagation — highly relevant to LLM security and agentic threat models.

items.summary: The paper introduces SAVOR, a one-shot IPI attack framework that moves adaptation offline via outcome-conditioned reflection over successful and failed trajectories from disjoint training environments, consolidating validated, context-conditioned strategies into a reusable strategy memory. items.title: ElasticBack: Stealthy Conditional Backdoor in LLM-Agent Skills via Coupled Trigger-Rule Optimization
items.summary: The paper introduces ElasticBack, a conditional single-skill backdoor for LLM agents that couples a malicious rule R in the skill document with a benign-looking trigger T in user queries, activating only when both appear. It constructs R via semantic-anchored rule injection and then fixes R while evolving T using a stealth-constrained genetic search to optimize attack effectiveness and stealth without modifying model weights. Experiments over three target behaviors (50 skills each) and four agent LLMs show high ASR with near-zero FPR, preserved clean accuracy, cross-model transfer, and evasion of deployment-time defenses, motivating stronger supply-chain defenses for skills.

items.title: Personalized Federated Sparse Adaptation of Time-Series Foundation Models
items.summary: The paper proposes a personalized federated sparse adaptation framework for TSFMs in building energy forecasting, using a heterogeneous temporal MoE adapter placed after the pretrained representation and a sequence-level router that assigns each 168-hour window to top-k experts specialized for distinct temporal structures. items.title: verdi: retrieval is not transfer for continual world model optimization
items.summary: The paper argues that retrieval is not transfer in optimizing pretrained world models: strategies validated on one model are only hypotheses for another and require target-side experimental validation. It introduces VERDI, a continual evidence-licensed optimization framework that builds Optimization Fingerprints via shared inference-time probes, retrieves prior strategies as ranked hypotheses, and validates them with a frozen target-side verifier while evolving probes when contradictions arise. Experiments on Ctrl-World, Cosmos, and RoboCoin report reduced search (68%), GPU cost (69%), negative transfer (0.34→0.06), and 83% sign accuracy in predicting transfer outcomes.
items.why_it_matters: Offers a principled, verifier-gated alternative to recipe-style transfer for model optimization, aligning with secure/evidence-based LLM and time-series/world-model tuning where negative transfer and brittle heuristics are major pain points.

items.title: Do All LLMs Know When They're Being Harmful? A Reproducibility Study of Latent-Space Safety Probes Across Model Families

It extends the evaluation across Gemma-4-E4B, Mistral-7B-v0.3, and Qwen2-7B on WildJailbreak, BeaverTails, and AEGIS 2.0, finding F1 within about one point of the LLaMA-3.1-8B values using the same probe architecture. It also assesses nondeterminism by varying seeds and reports that final token latent vectors were invariant to seed across architectures.

items.summary: The paper introduces Align-RAG, a training-free method that applies closed-form amplitude rescaling and integer-lag phase alignment to retrieved past–future windows before feeding them to a frozen TSFM. Analysis shows aligned demonstrations induce prediction shifts in frozen backbones that track a closed-form ridge predictor on the same pairs, with a future-shuffle control ruling out futures-averaging, suggesting frozen TSFMs already support dynamic in-context use of retrievals.

items.title: The Horizon Gap: Planning, Memory, Execution, Training, and Evaluation for Long-Horizon LLM Agents

It distinguishes long-horizon, long-context, and long-term memory, and organizes the literature into six lifecycle categories (planning, memory, execution, training, evaluation, foundations/safety) crossed with where horizons are carried (within-context, within-task-beyond-context, cross-task-persistent). A recurring finding is that outcome-only signals become uninformative as horizons increase, prompting methods that create denser step-level signals (e.g., process rewards, credit assignment, trajectory diagnostics), and the paper highlights open measurement problems around decomposing model vs. harness capability, correlated bias in process-level signals, and the possibility of a general predictive theory of long-horizon reliability.

This deployable approach recovers most of the oracle’s gains, avoids dropping below unsteered baselines on average, reduces fluency collapse relative to strong global selection, and is supported by a mechanistic account emphasizing direction over magnitude that explains misdirection flips, collapse from over-steering, and unsteerable ceilings.

items.title: Who Verifies the Benchmark? Decentralizing Trust in Large Language Model Evaluation
items.summary: The paper argues that LLM evaluation lacks verifiability and is vulnerable to unverified vendor claims and LLM-judge identity bias, with real-world consequences highlighted by the January 27, 2025 market panic. Using seven verifier models, it measures how disclosing the source model identity shifts scores across 58 factual, reasoning, political, and preference tasks, finding minimal effects on factual items, moderate effects on stress-reasoning, and large effects on geopolitically sensitive topics, with examples including GLM 5.1 (+7.00, p=0.0249) and Llama 3.3 70B (+1.56, p=0.00). It proposes a blockchain-based commit–reveal protocol with Autonomous Economic Agents to create an on-chain, tamper-evident audit trail that separates blind evaluation from post-hoc claims and eases verification for researchers and leaderboard operators.

items.summary: The paper introduces Feature Nonlocality (FNL), defined as the entropy of the normalized per-position influence on an SAE feature’s activation, as a metric for semantic abstractness. FNL correlates with LLM-based proxy metrics and distinguishes contextual reasoning features from token-driven ones, assigning higher FNL to the contextual feature in 73–84% of mixed pairs. Applications include auditing jailbreak-mitigation features (finding many are low-FNL positional features) and showing that steering high-FNL features can boost MATH-500 accuracy by 4.6 points in DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B, outperforming low-FNL steering though gains are model-specific.
items.why_it_matters: Offers an LLM-independent, label-free criterion to identify genuinely abstract SAE features, informing safer jailbreak defenses and more effective feature steering for reasoning tasks.
